Hardness will not tell you how it behaves

Rubber cannot be compressed in volume, only bulged sideways — so a thin wide pad is far stiffer than a thick narrow one of the same compound and hardness. Send us the load and the deflection you can allow, and we will set the shape and the hardness together.
It keeps sinking after you fit it

Rubber under permanent load creeps for years. We allow for it at the design stage rather than shipping a pad that meets its deflection on day one and sits 2 mm lower at year five, closing your clearances.
Natural rubber, unless the position rules it out

It has the best fatigue resistance we mix, which is why mounts are made from it. Where the pad is exposed or sees oil we move to neoprene and say why — the trade is fatigue life against weathering, and it should be a decision, not a default.
Bonded inserts, moulded in one piece
Most mounting pads need a steel plate or a bolt sleeve. We bond rubber to metal in-house, so the insert is moulded in rather than fitted afterwards, and there is no joint to work loose.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — but send us the load as well as the pad. A used pad has crept and measures thinner than it was moulded, so copying its dimensions reproduces a part that is already part-worn. We work back from what it has to carry and how far it may sink.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. Mark the load per pad, the deflection you can allow and the space available — those three, plus where the pad sits, are enough for us to quote. Hardness is our output, not your input.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house, and load-deflection is checked on batch samples against the approved drawing.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Pads ship unloaded and unstacked under compression.
